newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 6.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Industry and Trade Ministry is prepared to cancel the import deposit system as soon as it sees that the trade deficit has improved, but at this time it is too early, according to a director at the ministry, Milan Hovorka.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus participated in the international conference for the future of the world organised by the Swiss insurance company Winterthur in Montreaux, Switzerland.

- The ongoing conflict between the chairman of the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), Michael Zantovsky, and Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny over the army's preparations for NATO ended during yesterday's meeting of the Senate committee for foreign affairs.

- The chairman of the National Property Fund, Roman Ceska, is disturbed by the announcement yesterday from the chairman of the board at Poldi Steel, Josef Vostarek, who said Ceska is violating the agreement for respecting current property relations in the company and is attempting to turn around the positive developments at Poldi.

- ABB Energeticke Systemy s.r.o. signed a contract with Plzenska Teplarenska a.s. and Skoda TS s.r.o. for the supply of fluid boilers for the heating block in Plzen worth more than 1.5 million crowns.

PRAVO - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec, both from the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), made peace yesterday, after remarks from Zieleniec that Klaus was not keeping the cabinet informed. ODS decided to improve communication within the party and the coalition.
- The government wants to save between eight and 11 billion crowns on social aid next year, but the cuts still must be approved by parliament.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - According to the Finance Ministry, at the end of May, the pension system was lacking five billion crowns. Experts estimate the pension deficit could be 10 billion by the end of the year.

- The Finance Ministry proposed the cabinet immediately begin privatisation of the state's stakes in Komercni Banka and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka and begin looking from strategic partners for the two banks.

- The head of the economic institute CERGE-EI, Jan Svejnar, warned yesterday that three to five domestic banks are threatened with insolvency due to high interest rates on the monetary market, and the fate of these banks will depend on how long the central bank holds interest rates at high levels.
- According to Czech National Bank spokesman, Martin Svehla, the central bank should strengthen its reserves by obtaining a foreign loan of more than one billion dollars within the next few weeks.
- The unemployment rate at the end of May stood at 3.8 percent, which means that the unemployment office recorded 193,442 people without work, 1,581 more than in April.

LIDOVE NOVINY - After introducing a quota on imports of Czech beer, Slovakia is preparing similar measures for alcohol and other commodities, according to an announcement from Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar yesterday.
- A city court in Prague yesterday rejected proposals from large drug distributors to put General Faculty Hospital and Motol Hospital into bankruptcy.
- Skoda Plzen is leaving its plans to make Skoda Beta pick-ups in Lovec, Bulgaria, according to Nikolaj Ivancev from Hyundai, which represents Skoda in Bulgaria.

- The largest domestic munitions company, Aero Vodochody, into which McDonnell Douglas recently entered, should obtain a state guarantee for manufacturing 72 light L-159 fighter aircraft for the Czech Army.

- The state will receive nearly one billion crowns total in dividends for 1996 from Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna, about 700 million crowns from Komercni Banka and 250 million from Ceska Sporitelna.
